Caddy in front of the platform's apps, on ports 80 and 443: each app's domains reach its container, with HTTPS certificates Caddy gets and renews by itself. While an app is being replaced, Caddy holds its requests for up to 30 seconds instead of failing them. Behind Cloudflare's proxy it trusts only Cloudflare's addresses, and passes the visitor's own to the app in X-Forwarded-For. Sites of your own go in caddy/sites/*.caddy, which esquadro never rewrites.

```esquadro
blueprint caddy
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [server](../server/): the app must use them too.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | `""` | The email Let's Encrypt writes to about the certificates. |
| `certificates` | name | `"acme"` | acme: real certificates from Let's Encrypt; internal: Caddy's own, for a server no one reaches from the internet (a test). |
| `cloudflare` | bool | `true` | The domains are behind Cloudflare's proxy: trust its addresses. |

```esquadro
blueprint caddy {
  email ""
}
```

## Slots

Other blueprints add code at these points (see [Writing a blueprint](/esquadro/writing-blueprints/#slots)).

| Slot | |
|---|---|
| `caddy.sites` | Sites of other blueprints, as YAML list items indented by two spaces: "- domains: [grafana.acme.com]" then "  upstream: grafana:3000". |
